transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Time: 16:00 - 16:48 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Julia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Sana Ahmed (Redwood CSM), Ethan Ramirez (BlueGrid VP Product), Priya Nair (BlueGrid Cloud Architect), Tom Gallagher (BlueGrid Security), Lena Ortiz (BlueGrid Program Manager)
Recording note: call recorded; transcript auto-generated (some mis-hears likely)

Brief summary (auto):
- Kickoff to align on launch runway for BlueGrid's pilot using Redwood inference for customer support triage and energy demand forecasting models.
- Confirmed initial topology (hosted → dedicated trial → private/VPC if needed), success metrics (latency & cost), security requirements (SOC 2, KMS), and next steps for benchmarks and pricing.

Topics:
- Pilot scope and timeline
- Topology choices: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- Performance targets and benchmark plan
- Security/compliance checklist and KMS integration
- Onboarding runbook and sprint cadence

Action items (recap in-call): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Julia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give a quick agenda, do a run-of-runway alignment, then break into tech constraints. Sana and Marcus on deck for ops and benchmarks.
[00:20] Ethan Ramirez: Thanks Julia. We've got a tight window, Q4 pilot with a small user cohort then expand in Q1. Main ask is predictable latency for the triage model and cost control for the forecasting endpoints.
[00:34] Marcus Li: Got you. Quick clarifying question — are you expecting the triage calls to be single-turn generation or will you be doing multi-turn chat flows? That affects KV cache usage.
[00:48] Priya Nair: Mostly single-turn for triage, couple multi-turn for follow-ups. Also we plan to push embeddings for similarity search. We'll probably send a subset of requests to a forecasting model with longer sequences.
[01:10] Julia Park: Great. The usual pattern we recommend is start on hosted API to iterate, then move to Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for stable throughput, and optionally Redwood Private if you need VPC or on-prem. Is that the path you prefer?
[01:26] Lena Ortiz: Yes that's what we're thinking, we just need clarity on timelines and what the handoff looks like, especially networking and KMS.
[01:36] Tom Gallagher: On security, SOC 2 coverage and audit logs are musts. We also need to understand key rotation and HSM/KMS options. Can you give an overview?
[01:48] Marcus Li: Totally. Redwood provides KMS integrations with customer-managed keys — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and a bring-your-own HSM pattern. We log per-request metadata — token counts, model, latency — and those can be forwarded to your SIEM. I'll share a security one-pager after.
[02:08] Tom Gallagher: Cool, but do you do end-to-end encryption in flight and at rest with customer keys?
[02:14] Marcus Li: In transit is TLS; at rest we can encrypt with your KMS keys on private deployments. On hosted we encrypt at rest with Redwood-managed keys by default, and customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private. There was an auto transcript note: "KMS" sometimes transcribed as "CMS" so ignore those typos in the doc.
[02:36] Ethan Ramirez: For the pilot, our SLO target is median < 180ms for triage, p95 < 700ms, and cost target below $0.0025/token equivalent. Those numbers are rough but that's the bar.
[02:52] Marcus Li: Okay that's helpful. We'll test with similar sequence length distributions. For the triage model we usually see lower tokens per request, so batching and prefix caching will help the median. We'll propose a batch config in the benchmark worksheet.
[03:10] Priya Nair: On network topology, we plan to host the rest of our stack in us-west-2. We prefer the region low-latency routing. If Dedicated is in us-west-2 that'd be ideal.
[03:22] Julia Park: Redwood has infra in us-west-2 for Dedicated and a hosted endpoint close to it. For VPC peering with Private, we can do customer-managed VPC peering and private endpoints, but that step is typically later.
[03:36] Lena Ortiz: Re: runbook — can you run through what the onboarding sprint looks like? We want to set expectations for the first 6 weeks.
[03:44] Sana Ahmed: Sure. Typical onboarding sprint: Week 0 is discovery and environment access; Week 1 basic POC and smoke tests; Weeks 2–3 run benchmarks and calibration; Week 4 rollout pilot to small cohort; Weeks 5–6 iterate on prompts and scale. We'll deliver a runbook and checklist.
[04:02] Lena Ortiz: Nice. Does that assume Redwood will manage the Dedicated capacity or do we need a contract first?
[04:10] Julia Park: For Dedicated we do a reserved commit. We can provision a short trial window for benchmarks with credit-backed reserved, and then convert to monthly commit. We'll send pricing tiers.
[04:22] Ethan Ramirez: One issue is procurement cycles — we'll need finance sign-off on the commit. Ideally we want to run benchmarks and have rough cost numbers before committing.
[04:32] Julia Park: Absolutely — Marcus will provide a benchmark worksheet you can run off your sample traffic, and we can run back-of-envelope cost projections.
[04:40] Marcus Li: I'll also provide recommended quantization profiles for your forecasting model so you can see cost vs latency tradeoffs. Note that some quantization artifacts can affect downstream accuracy; we'll include eval metrics.
[04:56] Priya Nair: On private deployment: if we get to that stage, what's the timeline to go from Dedicated to Private? Is it weeks or months?
[05:06] Marcus Li: Usually 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals, KMS integration, and any air-gapped requirements. If you need on-prem we should budget more time.
[05:16] Tom Gallagher: For SOC 2 evidence we need encryption at rest with customer-managed keys and retention logs for 12 months. Do you support log export to a customer S3 or SIEM?
[05:26] Marcus Li: Yes, we can forward audit logs to a customer S3 bucket or push to Splunk/Datadog via our logging hooks. We'll include a sample log format in the security doc.
[05:36] Lena Ortiz: Can you also walk through who owns what during the onboarding? Team responsibilities.
[05:44] Sana Ahmed: From Redwood: AE for contract/pricing (Julia), SE for benchmarks and infra (Marcus), CSM (Sana) for onboarding coordination. From BlueGrid: Program lead (Lena) owns schedule, Cloud Architect (Priya) provides infra access, Security (Tom) handles compliance checklist, Product (Ethan) validates quality. We'll put a RACI in the runbook.
[06:06] Ethan Ramirez: Sounds good. A couple of risk items: 1) If p95 for triage is inconsistent, we may need a fallback synchronous route back to deterministic rules; 2) cost spikes if forecasting inference runs longer sequences than expected.
[06:22] Marcus Li: For risk 1, Redwood supports canary routes and automatic fallback policies to cheaper model variants or rule-based systems. We can configure a latency-based fallback at the routing layer. For risk 2, prefix-based KV cache and batching heuristics will reduce per-token costs; plus the benchmark will expose outliers.
[06:44] Priya Nair: Are there any hidden data residency constraints we should be aware of? We're operating in US only for now.
[06:50] Julia Park: For US-only workloads that's fine. If you expand to EU later, we can regionally pin models and routes.
[06:58] Tom Gallagher: On the security questionnaire, we have some bespoke encryption requirements — we'll paste them into the shared doc. What's the best way to share sensitive attachments?
[07:08] Julia Park: Email is okay for initial items; for high-sensitivity assets we prefer a secure S3 or your ticketing portal. We'll share a secure upload link in the runbook.
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: Can we talk about observability — how granular are the dashboards, can we get token-level breakout and per-model latencies?
[07:26] Marcus Li: The Redwood Console has per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and traces. We also have alerting on latency regressions and quality regressions tied to prompt sets. We'll give you a sample dashboard view.
[07:40] Ethan Ramirez: Great. For the forecasting model we care about 1) inference latency 2) tail latency 3) bit of accuracy regression when quantizing. Marcus mentioned evals — can you run an eval suite?
[07:52] Marcus Li: Yes, we can run evals against your prompt set — we'll need a sanitized sample set. We'll run accuracy baselines against the original FP model and the quantized variants and produce a delta report.
[08:04] Priya Nair: We'll scrub PII and deliver a dataset next week.
[08:08] Julia Park: Perfect. Let's talk pilot rollout cadence — you're aiming to start the pilot first week of November?
[08:14] Lena Ortiz: Targeting Nov 8 for pilot start, wanting two weeks of internal QA then go to a 1000-user cohort. Is that realistic?
[08:22] Marcus Li: Tight but doable if we get infra access and metrics this week. The critical path items are VPC peering (if private), KMS approvals, and benchmark results. For hosted→dedicated path it's faster.
[08:36] Ethan Ramirez: So action items to make that date: we will prioritize giving sample traffic to Marcus, Priya will confirm SLOs, Tom will answer security questionnaire, and Lena will lock stakeholders.
[08:50] Julia Park: We'll recap in the next steps; Marcus will send the benchmark worksheet and a short how-to. Sana will share runbook link and proposed sprint plan. I will send pricing and reserved commit options.
[09:02] Tom Gallagher: Quick procurement/Q: are there minimum commitment durations for Dedicated? We prefer short-term to start.
[09:12] Julia Park: We offer monthly reserved tiers and quarterly trials; we can do a short trial commit to run the benchmarks. We'll align with procurement on terms — Sana can loop in our contracts team.
[09:26] Priya Nair: On benchmarking, do you need us to run tests from our VPC or can Redwood run synthetic traffic?
[09:34] Marcus Li: Both are valid. We'll provide a JMeter/postman style harness you can run from your VPC to measure actual egress latency. Additionally, Redwood can run synthetic tests in-region for comparative numbers.
[09:48] Lena Ortiz: Are there any common gotchas you see during the first weeks? Anything we should preempt?
[09:54] Marcus Li: Top gotcha is not sampling the real token distribution — many teams run small tests and miss long-tail sequences. Another is forgetting model variant fallbacks in routes which leads to outages during spikes. We'll highlight those in the runbook.
[10:10] Ethan Ramirez: Okay let's go into a quick tech clarifying Qs — Marcus, you mentioned KV cache — how does that work in multi-tenant hosted scenario?
[10:20] Marcus Li: In hosted we do prefix-based caching with tenant isolation; we maintain per-tenant KV caches with TTLs. For Dedicated and Private, you get more control over cache sizing and TTLs. Some of the caching naming got transcribed odd in the raw notes as "KV cake" — ignore that.
[10:36] Priya Nair: For embeddings, what's the recommended dimensionality and batch size if we're doing similarity lookups in near real-time?
[10:44] Marcus Li: It depends on the vector store; for FAISS-style indices 768–1536 dims are common. We'll suggest embed configs and recommend batched upserts during off-peak to save costs.
[10:54] Julia Park: We're about halfway through time, is there anything else from BlueGrid side?
[11:00] Ethan Ramirez: Procurement will want to see a pilot scoping SOW and initial pricing. Also curious about support SLAs — do we get a named support contact during pilot?
[11:10] Sana Ahmed: During pilot you get CSM support and SE hours; for Dedicated contracts we include escalation and faster SLA windows. We'll include support packages in the pricing doc.
[11:20] Tom Gallagher: Can we get a sample SOC 2 attestation and an incident response runbook?
[11:26] Julia Park: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 redacted report and an incident process.
[11:32] Lena Ortiz: Next steps and owners — can we capture that now?
[11:36] Julia Park: I'll read them out: Julia sends pricing and reserved options (by 10/24); Marcus sends benchmark worksheet and run instructions (by 10/27); Sana shares onboarding runbook + sprint plan (by 10/25); BlueGrid provides sample traffic and SLOs (Priya & Ethan by 10/26); Tom to complete security questionnaire (10/28); Lena to confirm stakeholders and weekly cadence (10/23). Anything to add?
[12:00] Priya Nair: We'll also add an item: we'll try the initial synthetic test in us-west-2 and report results.
[12:06] Julia Park: Perfect. Any final questions?
[12:10] Ethan Ramirez: Nothing else, thanks all. Looking forward to the benchmark and sprint plan.
[12:16] Marcus Li: I'll follow up with a short video on how to run the harness.
[12:20] Sana Ahmed: And I'll drop the runbook link into the meeting notes: [link: onboarding-runbook-bluegrid] and the pricing stub.
[12:30] Julia Park: Great thanks everyone, we'll wrap.

End of meeting.
